prospect.name: Thomas Joseph
prospect.location: United States, Eastern time zone (407 area code)
prospect.occupation: Psychiatrist, works from home, 8-10 hours a day seeing patients
prospect.family_status: Married; wife pregnant with second child due 8 December; son Noah 20 months
prospect.training_background: Former athlete - soccer and basketball growing up; ran StrongLifts 5x5 with good results five or six years ago then fell off in months-long cycles; home gym with treadmill, barbell and plates; owns two adjustable kettlebells 12-32 kg; still plays pick-up basketball and soccer occasionally; negligible daily step count
prospect.medical: Pulled his lower back deadlifting around 220-245 lb about a year to eighteen months ago; never diagnosed - 'I never got diagnosed, you know, or anything' - self-rehabbed with preventative lower-back work; states no chronic pain now. Reports waking drained and low energy. No other conditions disclosed.

signals: Former athlete measuring himself against a past self - 'I don't want to believe that I've already peaked physically'
Lost ground to a hard season of work and young children rather than to illness
Explicit regret framing - 'gradually, you know, I see that I'm not able to do the same things I could anymore'
Wants athleticism back before the second child arrives, not marginal optimisation

goals.text: Get to the mid-160s at 10-12% body fat and have a six-pack again
Retain or recover the speed, quickness and agility he has lost
Steady energy through the day instead of being drained by the end of it
Be able to take Noah out and keep up with him once the second baby arrives
Set an example so his son develops a healthy lifestyle rather than a screen habit
Learn to programme for himself so he is set for life - 'teach a man to fish'

pains.text: Cannot sustain a routine - trains for a couple of months, falls off for six months to a year, repeats
No accountability - 'the biggest thing I was lacking all this time was accountability'
5x5 sessions ran to an hour and fifteen minutes, which his patient load will not absorb
Wakes drained and pushes through the day on preservation, which stops him training, which keeps him drained
Stress-eats sugar between patients - fruit snacks, Snickers
Dispenses exercise advice to patients all day and cannot follow it himself
Aches, pains and slow recovery after playing sport

objections.raw_quote: So, I mean, it's not like you can't do like 1,000 per month, you know, that sort of thing?
objections.rep_response: Quoted a monthly plan at $1,200 rather than $1,000 - 'it's going to be a little bit more expensive' - then, without isolating or running any financial-picture questions, offered to split it in half instead.

objections.raw_quote: Cause 6,000, I thought, so I didn't know it was gonna be 6,000. I thought, cause I, I, I'd read somewhere like on Reddit or something that was, it was like 200 a month and that's not the case.
objections.rep_response: Distinguished the $200/mo Primal University from one-to-one coaching - 'that's not one-on-one coaching... there's no programming to your needs'.

objections.raw_quote: So, so you're swearing by this, you're saying this, you will definitely get results if you, if you, if I stick with this program, right?
objections.rep_response: Answered with an absolute personal guarantee - 'Like I swear on my mother' - and then, to 'there's no chances this can fail', answered 'No way.'

objections.raw_quote: I mean, is there a reason why 30 days and why not three months?
objections.rep_response: 'That's how it's split.' Then agreed to ask - 'I will ask. I cannot promise, okay?' Left unresolved after payment was already taken.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Quoted $1,200 per month as the instalment rate before pivoting to a 50/50 split: $3,000 processed on the call, $3,000 in 30 days, stated as no interest. Prospect asked for the second payment at three months; rep said he would ask and could not promise.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: there's a guarantee with the six months. In those six months, if you follow everything to the T, you will add at least eight kilograms to your initial baseline weight of the kettlebell... If you would do all of that and didn't hit the eight kilos mark, Trevor is going to work with you until you hit that, yeah? For free.

evidence: First instalment processed live - 'Yeah. So it's processing payment now.' 'It's done. Let me, let me check that. Okay. We got it.'
Client agreement received, read aloud and signed on the call - 'So it's signed now.'
Onboarding call with Trevor booked for Monday 15th at 6:15 p.m. Eastern; Skool community join clicked
Counter-evidence: the second $3,000 is unpaid and the prospect immediately asked to move it out to three months, which the rep could not confirm
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor Monday 15th 6:15pm ET; complete onboarding questionnaire; rep to ask whether the second instalment can move to 90 days.

notable.note: The cleanest process in the batch and the only call where the agreement was actually signed live. Two things a manager should see. First, the rep answered a direct 'can this fail?' with 'No way' and 'I swear on my mother' - an absolute results guarantee far beyond the written +8 kg performance guarantee, given to a physician who read the contract's medical disclaimer aloud minutes later. Second, the rep quoted $1,200/month for an instalment plan on a $6,000 programme, which the sales manager himself criticised the next day: 'you use interest as the thing as to why he should do it, which I don't really love that frame.' An undiagnosed lower-back injury was disclosed and no clinician clearance was ever discussed.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion, especially in the second half - the whole checkout and agreement sequence from 00:45 to 00:52 has the rep's instructions under 'Thomas Joseph' and the prospect's reading of the contract under the rep. Roles read from content. Prospect not named in the title; recovered from the transcript and corroborated by the 2026-06-12 team meeting call review, where this same call is replayed by name. Rep's Fathom label reads 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)'; folder and batch name him Andrew Musial.
